mainTopic: How long a delay is allowed between writing and signing a גט, and what happens when a husband tells ten people to write a גט for his wife
overview: This amud opens by finishing an argument about a delay between writing a גט and signing it. One view worries that during the delay the husband may have made up with his wife, so it allows only a short gap. רבי יוחנן says even ten days is fine, because a reconciliation would become known. The גמרא then brings a new argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a husband who tells ten men to write a גט for his wife. Using a משנה, the גמרא shows that the case must be where he said 'all of you,' so all ten must sign. רבי יוחנן says only two are real עדים and the rest sign just to fulfill the husband's תנאי. ריש לקיש says all ten are real עדים. Their views differ in two cases: when only two signed on the day of writing and the rest signed later, and when one signer turns out to be a קרוב or פסול. Next comes a further dispute about an unfit person who signed first. The amud ends with a real case brought to רבי יהושע בן לוי, whose ruling begins on the next amud.

steps.title: The worry that the husband made up with his wife
steps.stepSummary: The first view explains why a long delay between writing and signing the גט is not allowed: maybe the husband reconciled with his wife in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are worried that perhaps he made up with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the opinion it was quoting just before this line. That opinion says that, according to רבי שמעון, a long delay before signing is not allowed, and this line gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that during the delay the husband may have reconciled with his wife and been together with her, which creates a problem for this גט. Because of that possibility, this view only accepts a short gap between writing and signing.

keyTerms.meaning: We are worried / we take into account the possibility
He made up with her; he reconciled with his wife

phrases.english: We are worried that perhaps he made up with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of an opinion begun just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A long delay between writing and signing is not allowed, out of concern that the husband reconciled with his wife.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן allows even a ten-day delay
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that according to רבי שמעון even a ten-day gap is fine, because a reconciliation would become public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: even from now until ten days later the גט is valid. If it were true that he had made up with her, the matter would have become known.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with the worry in Step 1. He says even a ten-day gap before signing does not ruin the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not dismiss the idea of reconciliation. He argues that if it had happened, people would know about it. Since nobody has heard of it, we can assume it did not happen.

keyTerms.meaning: From now until ten days later
If it were true
The matter has a 'voice'; it would become publicly known

steps.whatToRemember: The first view worries about a hidden reconciliation. רבי יוחנן says a reconciliation would not stay hidden, so even ten days is fine.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even from now until ten days later the get is valid;
if it were so that he made up with her,
the matter would have become known.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'the matter has a voice.' It means people would hear about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the worry stated in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a ten-day delay before signing is acceptable, because a reconciliation would have become public.

steps.title: Ten men told to write a גט: are they all witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: A new argument: if a husband tells ten men to write a גט, רבי יוחנן says two are real עדים and the rest sign because of his condition, while ריש לקיש says all ten are עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a man said to ten people 'Write a גט for my wife,' רבי יוחנן says two sign as עדים and all the rest sign because of the condition. ריש לקיש says all of them sign as עדים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. The question is what role the extra signers play when a husband asks ten men to handle his גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about why the extra people sign. רבי יוחנן says only two are real עדים and the others sign just to fulfill the husband's request (a תנאי). ריש לקיש says the husband meant all of them to be real עדים. Steps 4–6 show that both agree all ten must sign, because the husband said 'all of you.'

keyTerms.meaning: As witnesses: signing as a real witness
Because of the condition: signing only to fulfill the husband's request
ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן's colleague and frequent disputant

phrases.english: It was stated: if one said to ten people, "Write a get for my wife";

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁנַיִם מִשּׁוּם עֵדִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: two sign as witnesses,
and all of the rest sign because of the condition.
phrases.notes: The husband wanted everyone to sign, so the others sign to fulfill his wish, not as real witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כּוּלָּם מִשּׁוּם עֵדִים.
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said: all of them sign as witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new argument, unrelated in form to the delay discussion, though it will connect back to the ten-day idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: two of the signers are real עדים and the rest fulfill a תנאי. ריש לקיש: all signers are real עדים.

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation this argument is talking about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact situation behind the argument. This question sets up the next move, where the גמרא tests one possible case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before discussing why everyone signs, the גמרא needs to know why all ten have to sign in the first place. It depends on exactly what the husband said.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the case of the argument in Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly what the husband said that would require all ten to sign.

steps.title: It can't be where he didn't say 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the husband did not say 'all of you,' then rejects this from a משנה that says only one writes and two sign in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he did not tell them 'all of you,' didn't we learn in a משנה: if he said to ten people 'Write a גט for my wife,' one writes and two sign? So not all ten would need to sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible case and immediately challenges it from a משנה. It shows that this case cannot be the one they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband just said 'write a גט' without 'all of you,' the משנה says only one person writes and two sign. In that case there are no extra signers at all, so there would be nothing to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: proposes a possible case
All of you
But didn't we learn in a משנה? Introduces a challenge
Sign as witnesses

phrases.english: If you say that he did not say to them, "All of you";
but didn't we learn: if one said to ten people:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this מסכתא (66b).

phrases.english: "Write a get for my wife,"
one writes and two sign!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּלָא אֲמַר לְהוּ: ״כּוּלְּכֶם״; וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to Step 4 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the argument is about a husband who did not say 'all of you.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that in such a case only two sign, so there would be no extra signers to argue about.

steps.title: The case is where he said 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the argument is about a husband who said 'all of you,' where everyone must sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he said to them, 'All of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case. The husband told all ten, 'all of you write a גט,' so all ten must sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the husband says 'all of you,' everyone agrees all ten must sign. Now the argument in Step 3 makes sense: are the extra eight real עדים, or are they signing only because he asked?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces the corrected answer

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש is only where the husband said 'all of you.' Without those words, one writes and two sign.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said to them, "All of you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 after Step 5 ruled out the other option.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument might be about a plain instruction to ten people without 'all of you.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about where the husband said 'all of you,' so all must sign.

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two views, since both require all ten to sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when it would actually matter whether the extra signers are עדים or only fulfilling a תנאי. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש require all ten signatures. So the גמרא wants a case where their reasons lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the case now defined, asks for the practical difference between the two views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two views give different rulings.

steps.title: Two signed on the day, the rest within ten days
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up if two signed on the day of writing and the rest signed later within ten days. According to רבי יוחנן the גט is כשר, and according to ריש לקיש it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where two of them signed on that same day, and the others signed from then until ten days later. The one who says the others sign because of the condition holds the גט is valid. The one who says they all sign as עדים holds it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two views split. It is a גט where only two signed on the day it was written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the two real עדים signed on the right day, and the others fulfilled the condition later, so the גט is כשר. For ריש לקיש, all ten are עדים, and some עדים signed on a later day, so the גט is פסול. This ties back to the earlier discussion about delays in signing.

keyTerms.meaning: Two people
On its day: the same day the גט was written
And the others
Valid
Invalid

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says only two of the signers are real עדים, so if they signed on the day, later signatures don't hurt. ריש לקיש says all ten are עדים, so every one must sign on the day.
steps.confusionAlert: Even ריש לקיש does not say ten witnesses are always needed. Ten are needed only because the husband said 'all of you.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the role of a signer (real עד or only fulfilling a תנאי) decides whether a late signature ruins the גט.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where two of them signed on that day,
phrases.notes: 'That day' means the same day the גט was written.

phrases.english: and the others signed from then until ten days later.
According to the one who says they sign because of the condition, it is valid;
and according to the one who says they sign as witnesses, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ – דַּחֲתוּם בֵּי תְרֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ בְּיוֹמֵיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If two signed on the day of writing and the rest within ten days, רבי יוחנן rules the גט is כשר and ריש לקיש rules it is פסול.

steps.title: Another difference: one signer turns out to be a relative or unfit
steps.stepSummary: A second practical difference between the views: if one of the ten is a קרוב or פסול, the גט is כשר according to the view that the signatures are a תנאי, and פסול according to the view that they are all עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another difference: if one of the ten turns out to be a relative or disqualified. According to the one who says the signatures are because of a stipulation, the גט is valid. According to the one who says they are all witnesses, the גט is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second case where the two views about the ten signers lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the extra signers are only there to fulfill the husband's תנאי, an unfit signer does not hurt, because two fit עדים have still signed. If all ten are real עדים, then one unfit member ruins the whole group of witnesses, so the גט is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; another possibility
A relative, who may not serve as a witness
Disqualified or unfit; also means invalid
A condition set by the husband
Witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the dispute is about what the ten signers actually are: people fulfilling a condition, or true witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי – כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶם
phrases.english: Alternatively: for example, where one of them is found to be
a relative or disqualified.
According to the one who says it is because of the stipulation, it is valid;
according to the one who says it is because of witnesses, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי – כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶם קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 7, after the first answer in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between the two views?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If one signer is a relative or unfit, the גט is כשר according to the תנאי view and פסול according to the עדים view.

steps.title: An unfit person who signed first: two opinions
steps.stepSummary: Within the תנאי view, if a קרוב or פסול signed first, some say the גט is כשר because it is only a תנאי, and some say it is פסול because people may confuse it with ordinary documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a relative or disqualified person signed first, some say the גט is valid and some say it is invalid. Those who say valid hold that it is just a stipulation. Those who say invalid fear that people will confuse it with ordinary documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about a harder case: the unfit signer's name comes first, before any fit witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion follows the תנאי idea all the way: the order of names does not matter, since the extra names are not witnesses anyway. The second opinion worries that when people see an unfit signer at the top of a document, they may think unfit witnesses are acceptable in other documents.

keyTerms.meaning: At the beginning; first
People will come to confuse it
Ordinary documents

steps.confusionAlert: This disagreement is only within רבי יוחנן's תנאי view. According to ריש לקיש, an unfit signer makes the גט פסול anyway.

phrases.aramaic: אִי חֲתִים בִּתְחִילָּה קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל;
phrases.english: If a relative or disqualified person signed at the beginning;
phrases.notes: "At the beginning" means before two fit witnesses had signed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לָהּ כָּשֵׁר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: some say it is valid, and some say it is invalid.
Some say it is valid: it is just a stipulation;

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לַהּ פָּסוּל – אָתֵי לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי בִּשְׁטָרוֹת דְּעָלְמָא.
phrases.english: some say it is invalid: people will come to confuse it with ordinary documents.
phrases.notes: The worry is that people may start accepting unfit witnesses on regular documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי חֲתִים בִּתְחִילָּה קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the תנאי view from step 9 and tests it on a harder case: the unfit person signed first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute about an unfit signer who signed first: כשר because it is a תנאי, or פסול because people may confuse it with ordinary documents.

steps.title: A real case: the ten signers signed on different days
steps.stepSummary: A man told ten people to write a גט for his wife. Two signed that day and the rest signed over the next ten days. The case came before רבי יהושע בן לוי, and the גמרא begins his answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said to ten people: 'Write a גט for my wife.' Two of them signed on that day, and the others signed from then until ten days later. The man came before רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that matches the situation from step 8. It is setting up רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree: two signed right away and the rest signed later. The ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי will show how this case was decided in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain (person); opens a story
Write a גט for my wife
On that same day
And the others

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to ten people:
"Write a get for my wife";
two of them signed on that day,
and the others signed from then until ten days later.
phrases.notes: This is the same timing as the case in step 8.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
he said to him:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ לַעֲשָׂרָה: כִּתְבוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that matches the case in step 8, where the two views disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is presented here. רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling follows.
